blocks.text: Frequently Asked Questions About washer and dryer removal in Toronto

items.q: Q: Do you disconnect the washer and dryer before removing them?
a: A: Yes — disconnection is included in our service. We handle water supply lines, drain hoses, and electrical connections. For gas dryers, we disconnect the gas line safely before the unit is moved. You don’t need to touch anything before we arrive.

items.q: Q: How much does washer and dryer removal cost in Toronto?
a: A: Pricing depends on the number of units, appliance type, and access complexity. A single washing machine or dryer is a smaller load; a full set with pedestals in a condo suite on an upper floor involves more logistics. We give you a firm, all-inclusive quote on-site before anything moves. No surprise fees at the end.

items.q: Q: Can a landlord arrange washer and dryer removal without the tenant present?
a: A: Yes — we work with landlords and property managers regularly across Toronto for end-of-tenancy and rental property clearouts. As long as you have legal access to the property, we can coordinate the removal at a time that works for your schedule. Call us to discuss the details.

items.q: Q: Can you remove a stackable washer and dryer unit from a condo in Toronto?
a: A: Absolutely. Stackable units in condo laundry closets are one of the more common jobs we handle. We work within building access requirements, coordinate elevator bookings, and use protective pads on common area walls and floors. Just let us know it’s a stacked unit and a condo when you book.

items.q: Q: What happens to old washers and dryers after pickup — are they recycled?
a: A: Yes. Washing machines and dryers contain recoverable materials including steel, copper, and motor components, and we route them to certified recycling facilities in the Toronto area. If an appliance is still in working condition, we explore local donation options before it goes to processing.
